```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

necessary libraries
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(openxlsx)
```

load in gis master file data (so far)
```{r}
gismaster2 = read.csv("gisspreadsheet.csv", header = TRUE, colClasses = c(ZIP_code_GIS = "character"))
uniques = read.csv("uniquecitystatezip.csv")
```

we create a new column citystatezip, that shows each grants city, state, and zip in one string
```{r}
gismaster2$citystate = paste(gismaster2$city_GIS, gismaster2$state_GIS, sep = ", ")
gismaster2$citystatezip = paste(gismaster2$citystate, gismaster2$ZIP_code_GIS, sep = ", ")
```

we now connect each unique combo to their respective grant numbers. then we merge so that grant numbers are displayed on the unique combo file
```{r}
grant_lookup = gismaster2 %>%
  group_by(citystatezip) %>%
  summarize(
    grant_number = paste(grant_number, collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

uniques = uniques %>%
  left_join(grant_lookup, by = "citystatezip")
```

our dataframe now has the content we need, so we download and observe results in sheets
```{r}
write.xlsx(uniques, "realuniquecitystatezips2.xlsx")
getwd()
```
